title: A mother's empty heart
hook: Musa's mother's heart became empty, and Allah steadied it (28:10)

segments.voice: Yesterday: al-mudtarr, the cornered one whose call is heard. Your line was he answers the distressed. Today, a new surah.

Pharaoh is killing the newborn boys of the Children of Israel, and a mother has just had a son. By an inspiration from God, she's told to nurse him, and when she fears for him, to put him in a chest, as another surah tells it, and cast him into the river. Don't fear, don't grieve, the verse says: We will bring him back to you. So she sets her baby on moving water and lets go. Surah Al-Qasas, the Stories, the twenty-eighth, begins Musa's life with her. Then comes the next morning.

The Qur'an doesn't skip over what she felt. Pickthall: "And the heart of the mother of Moses became void". The Arabic is farigh: emptied out, vacant. Empty of what, commentators asked. Some said of everything except Musa; others, of patience, or of the calm she'd had the night before. She was about to give him away, the verse goes on, to blurt out that the child was hers, had God not strengthened her heart. The word there is rabatna, We tied: the verb for tying something fast so it doesn't drift. And the verse says why: so that she would be among the believers, those who trust. Notice what God doesn't do. He doesn't take the fear away. Her heart is still empty; He ties it so that it holds. Then she does something very practical. She tells Musa's sister, follow him. The girl watches from a distance as the child reaches Pharaoh's household. God had kept him from taking any wet nurse, so the sister steps forward: shall I show you a family who will look after him? So Musa comes home, fed at his own mother's breast, inside Pharaoh's household. The verse says it was so that her eye would be cooled and she wouldn't grieve, and so she would know God's promise is true. In this telling, faith isn't the absence of panic. It's a heart held steady while it's still afraid.
screen: `HER HEART BECAME EMPTY.` · `RABATNA: WE TIED IT DOWN.` · `THE SISTER FOLLOWS FROM AFAR.` · `HOME TO HIS MOTHER.`

segments.voice: Think of someone waiting for something frightening right now: results, a court date, a child far from home, a hospital bed. Hold their face in mind, and notice what they might need: not advice or cheerfulness, just someone beside them so their heart doesn't drift. If you pray, you can ask that their heart be tied steady.
Farigh. Empty, vacant: how Musa's mother's heart was left after the river, emptied of everything but her son, and held steady by God until he came home. Today's word.
Your line: a heart held steady. Fear and trust can live in the same heart. That's five hundred twenty-four days.

howItsDone: Muslims read the story of Musa's mother in Al-Qasas as a picture of trust in God under fear, and many recite its promise, We will bring him back to you, in times of separation.

original.note: Arabic: empty, vacant; the word for the heart of Musa's mother in 28:10.

trapdoor: what you thought: a brave mother who trusted God.
what it means: a mother whose heart was emptied by fear, and held steady by God so that she didn't fall apart.

what a scholar hears: fu'adu ummi Musa farighan, 'the heart of the mother of Moses became empty', then rabatna 'ala qalbiha, We bound her heart, and 28:13's cooling of the eye: the Qur'an keeps her fear in the story.

chat.says: If Musa's mother trusted God, why was her heart so empty?
options: Trust didn't remove her fear. God tied her heart steady while she was still afraid.
Her heart was empty because she had stopped trusting God's promise.
She was empty because she knew she would never see him again.
chat.meaning: Al-Qasas says her heart became empty, and God tied it, rabatna, so she would be among those who trust. The fear stayed; the heart held.

sources.quoted: And the heart of the mother of Moses became void
